notes: Sepolia (11155111) launch of the bounded PriorityQueue project. Token: LaunchToken (src/LaunchToken.sol), fixed supply of 1,000,000,000 tokens (10^27 minor units, 18 decimals) minted once in the constructor to msg.sender (the ProjectFactory); no constructor arguments, no owner, no mint, burn, pause or upgrade path. Application contract: PriorityQueue (src/PriorityQueue.sol), a bounded queue of at most 32 live entries (constant CAPACITY = 32). Each entry has a caller-chosen bytes32 id, its owner (the enqueuing msg.sender), a uint32 priority and a contract-assigned strictly increasing uint64 insertion sequence. Anyone may enqueue; only the entry's owner may cancel; anyone may pop the highest-priority entry, with equal priorities served FIFO by sequence. Duplicate live ids are rejected; a removed id may be re-enqueued with a new sequence. The constructor takes no arguments, is nonpayable and makes no external calls; the contract has no owner or privileged role, so $owner and $token are intentionally unused. It never references or moves the launch token. Runtime contains no DELEGATECALL, CALLCODE or SELFDESTRUCT. Compiler: solc 0.8.24, evm_version paris, optimizer 200 runs, bytecode_hash none, cbor_metadata false. Pool: launch token paired against native ETH (zero address), fee 3000, tickSpacing 60, no hook; initialPrice is sqrtPriceX96 1:1 and the deployer derives the effective opening price from the pinned policy. Tests (offline, forge test): unit tests for capacity, cancellation in every position, priority ties, and fuzz/invariant tests of arbitrary operation sequences against a naive sorted-array model; see README.md and REVIEW.md.
